documentation.title: Free impact of two deformable spheres
documentation.description:
A transient 3D impact between two free deformable SPHERES, with no applied load and nothing holding either body up. A contact patch forms, grows and releases.
NOTHING IS FIXED. That is the point, and it is what every other contact testcase gives up: a body held by a Dirichlet condition has its equilibrium supplied by the boundary, so the contact force is whatever balances a known load. Here the only force in the model is the contact traction, and the motion is supplied entirely by an initial velocity on one sphere. Expressing that needed an initial VELOCITY for a mechanic PDE, which was a schema gap rather than missing code -- note that quantity names the DERIVATIVE field (quantity="mechVelocity"), and that initialValues must come after contactList.
WHAT IT ASSERTS
1. contactForceX = contactForceY = 0. The impact is head-on and the model is symmetric about the z axis in geometry, mesh and initial condition alike, so the contact traction can have no net transverse component; contactForceZ carries the whole of it. Exact, independent of material, time step and mesh, and a real check on the implementation: a mispaired point or a normal taken from the wrong facet breaks the symmetry immediately. This is the 3D form of the invariant, with two components to satisfy rather than one. 2. The contact state at the final step. Recorded, not predicted -- an impact has no closed-form contact force. What makes it worth asserting is that a free transient impact reaches a definite contact state at all. 3. That the run completes, which with no load and no support is not a formality.
The patch is a few points wide: the sphere is faceted and the Hertzian patch is comparable to a facet, so this demonstrates a free impact between curved deformable bodies but does NOT resolve a Hertzian pressure distribution, and nothing here asserts one.
resStopCrit is deliberately loose and convergence is judged on incStopCrit: a free impact has no external load, so the residual has nothing to normalise against and falls back to an absolute value that is unreachable. normalSmoothing="nodal" because the sphere's surface is faceted and the patch sits right on top of the normal jumps.
